_comment: forest_tree: Map 3's tower, a great tree grown into a shape, and the sagging middle of the level's roof. Origin is the Tower node (world y 25.35) so it drops in at identity: the trunk stands in the water 25 m below, the lattice of eight branch piers and pointed arches between y 11 and 25.6, the scalloped leaf canopy y 24.8..27.0, the guard's flat floor at y 27.05 (origin + 1.70, as map 1) inside a 0.55 m leaf sill, six thin branches leaning in over it with leaf clumps for a partial roof. From the crown's rim (r 11, y 34.1) a leaf sheet sweeps OUT AND UP over the ravine to the level's seam (forest_seam: r 47.6, 240 shared points, y 50.0 mean) -- a 15.9 m climb, so the tree is the low middle of a dome that is high at the ring. Eighteen rings on forest_seam.SHEET's curve (its nine, split where a band would be a ribbon too coarse to carry the billow), billowing up to +-0.46 m and handing that billow over to the seam's own wave over the last 9 m of radius, so no ring can climb past the next one out. The sheet's underside is many tree tops of all sizes and shapes hanging from the dome, creased where they meet, the tower's crown one of them; small clumps hang in the creases, clear of the guard's eye at 28.7. A coarse top skin runs back from the same seam ring into the crown, so the sheet is a closed leaf mass and no edge carries three faces. The collider gains the sheet as a 24-gon ring on every forest_seam.SHEET radius (r 11 out to 47.6), so a shot fired up over the ravine stops on the dome's own curve instead of on a chord under it. One material (the forest atlas), one mesh. ForestTreeCollision is the purpose-built collider shipped as a `-colonly` node (floor, sill, canopy slope, trunk, sheet); Godot turns it into a StaticBody3D + ConcavePolygonShape3D and drops its mesh, so `surfaces` counts only what is drawn.
